cards.front: Recall a key point about Romantic Music 1815-1910
cards.back: Romantic music prioritised emotional expression: chromatic harmony, rubato, wider dynamic range and thicker textures created intensity and drama.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Romantic Music 1815-1910
cards.back: Chopin's piano music uses rubato (flexible tempo), elaborate ornamentation and harmonic chromaticism — it demands expressive, personal interpretation.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Romantic Music 1815-1910
cards.back: The Romantic orchestra expanded significantly: more brass (trombones, tuba), more woodwind (piccolo, cor anglais, bass clarinet), harp and percussion.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Romantic Music 1815-1910
cards.back: Late Romantic Requiems (Verdi, Fauré) combined liturgical text with dramatic orchestration — sacred music with theatrical emotional power.

cards.front: What should you know about music exam tips?
cards.back: Identify Romantic features: chromatic harmony, rubato, expanded orchestration, programmatic elements. Compare with Classical style. Explain how features reflect Romantic values.

Students often make mistakes here. Wrong: Romantic music is just classical music that is more emotional. Correct: Romantic music has SPECIFIC identifiable features: chromatic harmony (moving beyond diatonic chords), expanded orchestration, programmatic elements (music telling stories), rubato, thicker polyphonic textures, and nationalism. These are distinguishable features the exam tests you on.

Compare a Romantic piano piece by Chopin with a Classical piano piece by Mozart. Identify at least three differences in musical elements and explain how each reflects the change from Classical to Romantic style.
AO1 — Knowledge: Show knowledge of Romantic Music 1815-1910 using appropriate musical vocabulary (e.g. terminology for elements, devices, and contexts).

cards.back: Understanding romantic music 1815-1910 informs your performing (AO1) and composing (AO2) work. In performance, awareness of romantic music 1815-1910 helps you make interpretive decisions that serve the music. In composition, romantic music 1815-1910 provides the building blocks of your creative work — the choices you make about this element shape the identity and coherence of your piece.

cards.front: Exam Technique for Romantic Music 1815-1910 Questions
cards.back: In the AQA GCSE Music listening exam, questions about romantic music 1815-1910 typically ask you to: identify features by ear; describe how they are used; explain their effect; compare features between extracts. The key to success is precise terminology — never use vague language.
